caveats:
The area of interest is the observed flood extent of 27 August 2026 widened by 200
metres. The flood extent is an interpretation of imagery for a single date rather than
a surveyed boundary, and water levels changed through the event.

OpenStreetMap coverage reflects where volunteer mappers have been active and changes
between updates. Overture layers combine several upstream sources, some of them machine
generated. Cross-check critical decisions with local field knowledge.
dataset_source: OpenStreetMap contributors, Overture Maps, volunteer field reports
name: hot_flood_npl
notes:
OpenStreetMap and Overture Maps vector layers for the area flooded in the 2026 Bhote
Koshi and Trishuli flood in Nepal, and the ground immediately around it.

The area of interest is the observed flood extent of 27 August 2026 widened by 200
metres. The extent itself was mapped from drone, Landsat, PlanetScope and Sentinel
imagery and is published here as its own resource, so the water line can be separated
from the margin around it. That margin brings in buildings and roads beside the water,
so a feature being in this dataset is not evidence that it was flooded or damaged. Clip
to the Flood Extent resource when you need figures for the water itself.

The area follows the river from Rasuwagadhi to the Narayani confluence, across Bagmati
and Gandaki Provinces and the districts of Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha and Chitawan.

Every layer holds what is standing and what has been lost, so buildings and roads do not
vanish from a download once mappers record them as destroyed. `status` says Standing,
Damaged or Destroyed, and the Destroyed and Damaged Features layer gathers everything
marked destroyed or damaged in one place.

Most layers come in two versions. The OpenStreetMap ones are rebuilt straight from
OpenStreetMap through the day, so they carry volunteer work as it lands. The Overture
ones fuse Microsoft, Google and OpenStreetMap, which reaches ground volunteers have not
mapped yet, but they follow Overture's own release cycle and will not show mapping done
during this response. Overture is wider, OpenStreetMap is current: for damage work
prefer OpenStreetMap and use Overture where its coverage is thin.

Mapping task boundaries from the Tasking Manager campaign show where volunteers are
being asked to map. The bridge damage assessment is reported from the ground by
volunteers and lists road bridges with their condition after the flood, deck length
where measured, and administrative codes from the same boundaries as the other layers.

For the wider 1 km river corridor under assessment, use [Nepal Flood 2026 River
Corridor](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/hot_flood_npl_corridor). AI-scored building
damage from post-event imagery is published separately as [Nepal Flood 2026: fAIr
Damage Assessment](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/hot_flood_npl_buildings_damage).

Subscribe to the dataset for updates as mapping progresses.

- Source: [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/), [Overture Maps](https://overturemaps.org/), NAXA and volunteer field reports
- Part of HOT disaster response exports on HDX by [HOT](https://www.hotosm.org/)

**For up-to-the-minute exports from OpenStreetMap in a variety of formats for GPS and GIS, visit http://export.hotosm.org**

Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team (HOT) acts as a bridge between the traditional humanitarian responders and the OpenStreetMap Community. HOT works both remotely and physically in countries to assist the collection of geographic data, usage of that information and training others in OpenStreetMap.

resources.description: Mapping task boundaries for the Tasking Manager campaign "2026 Nepal Floods". Status included: ARCHIVED, PUBLISHED. Each feature is one Tasking Manager project boundary and carries its id, name, status, priority, organisation, mapping types, completion percentages, contributor counts and a link to the project. This layer shows where volunteers are being asked to map, which is not the same as where data exists: a project at low completion marks a known gap rather than coverage. Regenerated daily from the Tasking Manager API, so the percentages track live progress. Source: HOT Tasking Manager (https://tasks.hotosm.org/).
